diagnostic_evidence.quote: These three rows form the three $2 \times 2$ submatrices of $\hat{C}$ with the smallest singular value equal to $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n-1}}$.
In terms of matrix $M$, it can be achieved only if $M$ is non-negative (but not positive).
which finalizes the proof of the equality criteria.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition pr asserts an 'if and only if' criterion, but the equality analysis only derives the clustered structure from equality (necessity). The paper never shows that a clustered configuration actually attains max sigma_2^2 = 1/n. Such a configuration has groups p,q,r, |w|=1/(2n)+1/(2p) etc., and px+qy+rz=0. The same unproved fact is used inside the induction. Case A asserts that each of the three cross-group 2x2 submatrices of C-hat attains sigma_2 = 1/sqrt(n-1). The inductive hypothesis supplies only the clustering and the fact that the maximum equals 1/sqrt(n-1). If only one cross-group pair attained the maximum, switching to 'one of the other two submatrices' would be unjustified, and the strictness argument would fail.

failure_location.quote: The corresponding equality is achieved if and only if the rows of the matrix are clustered into three non-empty groups

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the verification. For rows from different groups, sigma_2^2 = (|x|+|y|-|x+y|)/2 by (sqdot). From px+qy+rz=0 with A=p|x|, B=q|y|, C=r|z|, the law of cosines gives 1-cos(x,y) = (A+B-C)/(AB) with A+B-C = 1-r/n. This yields |x+y| = |x|+|y|-2/n, so every cross-group pair has sigma_2^2 = 1/n, while same-group pairs are singular. Alternatively, observe from the Case B analysis that the cross-block entries of M vanish, i.e. P(1/n)=0 for every cross pair.
issues.overall_effect: The 'if' half of the equality criteria in pr and co is unproved. The Case A strictness step, on which the 'only if' half depends, rests on an unjustified premise.
issues.title: Sufficiency of the equality criterion is never proved, and Case A relies on it
issues.why_classification: A short routine computation closes both gaps, and every stated claim survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then the three $2 \times 2$ matrices composed of these vectors as rows have pairwise different first (and second) right-singular vectors.
Thus, the conjugated square of the first right-singular vector is oriented as the sum of the squares of vectors $v_i$ and $v_j$.
By Lemma \ref{le} vector $(\pm 1, 0)^T$ can be a right-singular vector of at most one of these three submatrices.

issues.failure_explanation: Pairwise non-collinear squares do not imply pairwise non-collinear sums. Take v_1=(1,0), v_2=(1,1)/sqrt2 and any v_3 with v_3^2=(-1/2,1/2). The squares (1,0), (0,1), (-1/2,1/2) are pairwise non-collinear, yet v_1^2+v_2^2=(1,1) and v_1^2+v_3^2=(1/2,1/2) are positively parallel. M^T M = ((|v_i|^2+|v_j|^2)/2)I + (1/2)[[s1,s2],[s2,-s1]] with s=v_i^2+v_j^2, so the matrices with rows (v_1,v_2) and (v_1,v_3) share both right-singular vectors, and the lemma's conclusion is false. The arctan formula also fixes only the line of s, not which singular vector is first. The claim fails even in the Case A configuration. With p'=2, q'=r'=1 we have 2x+y+z=0, so x+y=-(x+z): the sums are collinear, and (±1,0) can be a right-singular vector of two submatrices (first of one, second of the other).

failure_location.quote: their sums $v_1^2 + v_2^2$, $v_1^2 + v_3^2$ and $v_2^2 + v_3^2$ are pairwise non-collinear too

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma under an extra hypothesis: alpha v_1^2+beta v_2^2+gamma v_3^2=0 for some alpha,beta,gamma>0. This holds in Case A because p'x'+q'y'+r'z'=0. Then each v_i^2+v_j^2 lies in the open sector spanned by v_i^2 and v_j^2, and the three sectors are disjoint, so the sums are pairwise not positively parallel. Since the sigma_2 right-singular vector u has u^2 positively parallel to -(v_i^2+v_j^2), the three sigma_2-vectors are distinct. Use only this weaker conclusion in Case A.
issues.overall_effect: The Case A strictness argument rests on a false lemma. Hence the necessity part of the equality criteria in pr and co is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Lemma le is false: non-collinear squares do not give non-collinear or distinctly oriented pair sums
issues.why_classification: The stated lemma is false. It must be weakened with a new hypothesis and re-proved by a different (though short) argument. The main proposition survives with this contained fix, without global restructuring.
